lead.headline: Amazon cargo jet overruns Miami runway, hits vehicles; 5 dead
lead.dek: The Boeing 767 freighter from San Juan left the runway at about 128 mph and burned; the NTSB briefs Monday
body: Prime Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 freighter operated for Amazon by 21 Air, ran off Runway 30 at Miami International Airport after landing from San Juan, Puerto Rico, at about 2 p.m. Sunday, struck vehicles on a road beside the airfield and burned, killing five people and injuring five, officials said.

ABC News reported the jet left the runway at about 128 mph and came to rest on its side in a field with a fuel leak and, Fire Chief Raied Jadallah said, a "very complex fire" in the engines. About 200 fire-rescue personnel responded; three of the injured were critical. NBC News said the two pilots were among the dead, which CBS Miami said officials had not confirmed.

The 32-year-old aircraft was delivered as a passenger jet in 1994 and converted to cargo in 2015. The airport halted arrivals for about three hours and reopened two of four runways by 5 p.m.; about 250 flights were delayed. The NTSB sent a go-team led by Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy, who is to brief reporters Monday. Amazon said it was "heartbroken."

briefs.headline: Kauai closes parks, opens refuge areas as Lowell turns north
briefs.summary: Kauai County shut all parks and campgrounds from 5 p.m. Sunday and opened five refuge areas as Lowell, a Category 3 with 120 mph winds, was forecast to pass west of the island Monday night.

briefs.headline: Administration asks Supreme Court again on mail-ballot rule
briefs.summary: An emergency application filed Sunday seeks to let the Postal Service enforce its mail-ballot tracking rule after Judge Indira Talwani's Friday injunction; North Carolina began mailing ballots last week.

briefs.headline: CENTCOM calls Iran's claim of hitting a U.S. drone vessel a lie
briefs.summary: Spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins called the Guard's Sunday claim "a total lie," CBS News reported; Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration is "always open" to nuclear talks.

briefs.headline: Republicans open a two-day midterm convention in Dallas Wednesday
briefs.summary: The first midterm-year national convention runs Sept. 9-10 at American Airlines Center with 109 speakers; JD Vance headlines the first night and President Trump closes the second.

briefs.headline: AfD wins 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt, three seats short of a majority
briefs.summary: Alternative for Germany took a projected 39 of 83 seats in Sunday's state election; Chancellor Merz's CDU fell to 17.2%, and state premier Sven Schulze said it will not cooperate with the AfD.

briefs.headline: Nepal mourns flood dead as 500 workers feared trapped in tunnels
briefs.summary: Flags flew at half-staff Monday for the victims of last month's floods, which killed more than 1,300 in Nepal and Tibet; about 900 hydropower workers are missing and some 500 are believed trapped in tunnels.

briefs.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least four in southern Lebanon
briefs.summary: Israel said Sunday's strikes in the Nabatieh district answered two Hezbollah drones; Lebanon's health ministry counted at least four dead and 20 wounded, and President Joseph Aoun asked Washington to halt the attacks.

briefs.headline: Cape Verde mourns 25 killed in school excursion bus crash
briefs.summary: A bus carrying 32 people back from the Pico do Fogo crater veered into a ravine on Fogo Island late Saturday, Africanews reported; most of the dead were children, and President Jose Maria Neves ordered an inquiry.

briefs.headline: State asks high court to bar neglect claims over jail deaths
briefs.summary: Corrections and the attorney general want the Supreme Court of Appeals to drop "deliberate indifference" as grounds for damages over inmate deaths; two cases are set for argument Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Bluefield State student dies after incident at Brush Creek Falls
briefs.summary: The university said a student died after a Saturday incident at the falls; local and state authorities conducted search and recovery, and the name was withheld at the family's request.

briefs.headline: Man in his 70s dies in Friday night house fire near Belle
briefs.summary: His wife and son were burned after going back in for pets, Belle Fire Chief David Fletcher said; the fire on Witcher Creek Road appeared to start near the electrical box.

briefs.headline: Marmet marks Labor Day with festival tied to Blair Mountain march
briefs.summary: The festival of more than 70 years drew more than 60 vendors Sunday; Mayor Frances Armentrout noted the 1921 march to Blair Mountain began in the town, and the parade is set for 10 a.m. Monday.

regional.item: Huntington begins $10 special-event parking Sept. 15 in 60 spaces near Marshall's stadium, starting with the Sept. 26 home game.
Parkersburg council takes final readings Tuesday on a $25.7M PFAS water-filtration project funded largely by $17.8M from the Chemours settlement.
The 56th Nicholas County Potato Festival runs Friday and Saturday, Sept. 11-12, in downtown Summersville with a parade, fireworks, a 5K and eating contests.
Preservation Thurmond says about a dozen historic buildings in and around Thurmond face demolition and only three can be saved through leases.

away.item: The $6.45M five-way roundabout on Route 67A at the Bennington College entrance was substantially complete Aug. 7, and VTrans said Aug. 31 it is taking feedback by survey.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Fair is listed to run Wednesday through Saturday, Sept. 9-12, at Camp Caesar in Cowen, according to its carnival operator's schedule.
Surf City on Aug. 31 put out a request for appraisers for its Coastal Storm Risk Management beach-nourishment project, with proposals due Oct. 2.

briefs.headline: Seven run for Prince George mayor ahead of Friday's deadline
briefs.summary: Seven mayoral and 13 council candidates have filed for the Oct. 17 civic election, incumbent Simon Yu among them; nominations close at the end of business Friday, Sept. 11.

briefs.headline: AI 'Cat in the Hat' threat posts reach Fort St. James
briefs.summary: RCMP, School District 91 and the Education Ministry are looking into AI-generated horror posts naming students; police said no crime is apparent so far.

briefs.headline: Victoria council files objection to West Coast oil pipeline
briefs.summary: Council voted to tell Ottawa it opposes the 1,250-km line carrying up to 1 million barrels a day before a Sept. 18 federal deadline; MP Aaron Gunn said it should "stay in its lane."

briefs.headline: Bear attack near Whistler sends hiker to hospital by air
briefs.summary: Three hikers met two bears near Conflict Lake in the Callaghan Conservancy on Friday; one woman had non-life-threatening injuries, and conservation officers killed an adult male black bear.

briefs.headline: Canada's counter-tariffs on U.S. goods take effect Tuesday
briefs.summary: Duties of 15 to 50 per cent on $27.6 billion in U.S. imports start at 12:01 a.m. Sept. 8; no formal talks have been held since Aug. 21, the Globe and Mail reported.

briefs.headline: Woman, 46, dies as 200 mm of rain floods Cape Breton
briefs.summary: Her body was found in Richmond County after her car was left on a flooded bridge Saturday; about 40,000 customers lost power and three counties declared emergencies.

briefs.headline: Isar Aerospace's Spectrum reaches orbit from Norway
briefs.summary: The 28-meter rocket lifted off from Andoya on Saturday and put small satellites and an experiment in orbit, ESA said, in the first orbital launch from continental Europe; Isar's first flight failed last year.

briefs.headline: Extreme pressure turns blue pigment into 4,000-atom copper chains
briefs.summary: Squeezing copper phthalocyanine above 21 gigapascals produced single-atom copper chains more than 4,000 atoms long, against a prior record of 28, researchers reported in Science.

briefs.headline: Cancer drug strengthens bones, cuts fat in menopausal mice
briefs.summary: University of East Anglia researchers reported in npj Drug Discovery that CADD522 strengthened bone and cut weight and fat in post-menopausal mice on identical diets; it has not been tested in people.

briefs.headline: SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg
briefs.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off Sunday at 10:26 a.m. EDT after a one-day slip; booster B1088 landed on a drone ship on its 19th flight in the 103rd Falcon 9 mission of 2026, Space.com reported.

briefs.headline: Authors dispute publisher claims on Anthropic settlement
briefs.summary: Authors say publishers and literary agencies are claiming shares of Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement, which pays $3,000 per pirated title, TechCrunch reported; Writer Beware called the reports "widespread and systemic."

briefs.headline: Chatbots wrongly reassure resistant sleep apnea patients
briefs.summary: In 700 simulated consultations, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek and Grok gave correct referral advice every time to cooperative patients but only 64% of the time when patients pushed back, King's College London researchers said.

briefs.headline: Thailand pauses data center builds while it writes rules
briefs.summary: Thailand's National Economic and Social Development Council halted data center construction and approvals, gave operators a week to report facilities and said sites above 2 MW will be classed as industrial, The Register reported.

weather_ear: The Weatherman has the forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Putnam and Kanawha ran no regional line; the Belle fire and the Marmet festival run as statewide briefs. It is Labor Day.
